The Hindi total then gives the Hindi-and-Sanskrit-only region as 49, and the Sanskrit total gives the Sanskrit-only region as 40. Adding all seven regions gives 291. Adding the three subject totals, or forgetting the all-three region, gives the other options.

items.question: If x = sqrt(11 + 2 sqrt(10)) + sqrt(11 - 2 sqrt(10)), what is the value of x^2 + 1/x^2?
items.explanation: Squaring gives x^2 = 11 + 2 sqrt(10) + 11 - 2 sqrt(10) + 2 sqrt(121 - 40) = 22 + 18 = 40. Then x^2 + 1/x^2 = 40 + 1/40 = 1601/40. Subtracting the reciprocal instead of adding gives 1599/40.

items.question: If sin A + cos A = 6/5, what is the value of sin^3 A + cos^3 A?
items.explanation: Squaring gives sin^2 A + cos^2 A + 2 sin A cos A = 36/25, so sin A cos A = 11/50. Then sin^3 A + cos^3 A = (sin A + cos A)^3 - 3 sin A cos A (sin A + cos A) = 216/125 - 99/125 = 117/125.

items.question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point on the ground is 30 degrees. After moving 36 m towards the tower, the angle of elevation becomes 60 degrees. What is the distance from the second position to the top of the tower?
items.explanation: Let the height be h. From the first point, the distance to the base is h divided by tan 30, and from the second point it is h divided by tan 60. The difference is 36 m, so h times (the square root of 3 minus 1 over the square root of 3) = 36, giving h = 18 times the square root of 3 m. The slant distance from the second point is the square root of h squared plus (h over the square root of 3) squared, which is 2h over the square root of 3 = 36 m. The height itself, 18 times the square root of 3 m, is the trap.

items.question: What is the value of x? Statement I: x^3 - x = 0. Statement II: x^2 = 1.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives x equal to 0, 1 or -1, and statement II gives x equal to 1 or -1. Together they still leave two values, 1 and -1, so the statements together are not sufficient. The trap is that combining two equations feels decisive even when two cases survive.

items.question: What is the present age of A? Statement I: The ratio of the present ages of A and B is 5 : 6. Statement II: After 4 years, the ratio of their ages will be 6 : 7.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only the ratio, and statement II gives only a future ratio. Together they fix the ages: if A is 5k and B is 6k, then (5k + 4) / (6k + 4) is 6/7, giving k equal to 4, so A is 20. Each statement alone leaves the scale unknown.

items.question: Is P the sister of Q? Statement I: P is the daughter of R. Statement II: Q is the son of R.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only that P is R's daughter, and statement II gives only that Q is R's son. Together they make P and Q the children of the same parent, so P is Q's sister, and both statements together are sufficient. Either statement alone leaves the family link unknown.

items.question: What is the volume of a cube? Statement I: Its side is a prime number of centimetres. Statement II: Its volume is between 100 and 150 cubic cm.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone allows any prime side, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone allows any volume in the range, so it is not sufficient. Together, the side must be prime and its cube must lie between 100 and 150, which only the side 5 cm satisfies, giving a volume of 125 cubic cm, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the average weight of five people? Statement I: The average weight of the first four people is 68 kg. Statement II: The fifth person weighs 82 kg.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only the first four weights as a total of 272 kg, and statement II gives only the fifth weight. Together they give the total as 354 kg, so the average is 70.8 kg. Each statement alone leaves part of the group unknown.

items.question: A faulty clock was set right at noon on Monday. What time will it show at 12 noon on Wednesday? Statement I: The clock gains 2 minutes every hour. Statement II: It was set right at 12 noon on Monday.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: From 12 noon on Monday to 12 noon on Wednesday is 48 hours. The clock gains 2 minutes an hour, so it gains 48 x 2 = 96 minutes, which is 1 hour 36 minutes, and it therefore shows 12 noon plus 1 hour 36 minutes, which is 1:36 PM. Statement I alone gives the rate but not the starting time, and Statement II alone gives the starting time but not the rate, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What day of the week was 14 November 2026? Statement I: 1 January 2026 was a Thursday. Statement II: 2026 is not a leap year.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone does not fix the day, because the number of days in February is unknown: in a leap year 14 November would fall one day later. Statement II alone says nothing about any day of the week. Together, 2026 has 365 days with February having 28 days, so 14 November is 317 days after 1 January, and 317 days after a Thursday is a Saturday, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: How many students play both cricket and hockey? Statement I: 70 play cricket and 60 play hockey. Statement II: There are 110 students in all and 5 play neither game.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: From statement II, 105 students play at least one game. Adding the two game counts gives 130, so the overlap is 130 minus 105, which is 25. Both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the area of a square? Statement I: The side of the square is a whole number of centimetres. Statement II: The area is between 130 and 160 square cm.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone allows any whole-number side, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone allows any area in the range, so it is not sufficient. Together, the side must be whole and its square must lie between 130 and 160, which only the side 12 cm satisfies, giving an area of 144 square cm, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: Is n divisible by 15? Statement I: n is divisible by 3. Statement II: n is divisible by 5.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone leaves the factor 5 unchecked, and statement II alone leaves the factor 3 unchecked. Together they settle it, since 3 and 5 are coprime and their product is 15, so both statements together are sufficient. The trap is that either divisibility alone feels close to enough.

items.question: Is y divisible by 9? Statement I: y is a perfect square. Statement II: y is divisible by 3.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone allows squares such as 4, 9, 16 and 25, some divisible by 9 and some not, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone allows multiples of 3 such as 3, 6 and 12, some divisible by 9 and some not, so it is not sufficient. Together, y is a square divisible by 3, so 3 divides its square root and 9 divides y, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: What is the distance covered by a car? Statement I: The car covers the first stretch at 80 km per hour for 2 hours. Statement II: The car covers the second stretch at 100 km per hour for 1 hour.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I alone gives only the first stretch, 160 km, so it is not sufficient. Statement II alone gives only the second stretch, 100 km, so it is not sufficient. Together, the distance is 160 + 100 = 260 km, so both statements together are sufficient.

items.question: Can we conclude that Ravi is a doctor? Statement I: All doctors wear white coats. Statement II: Ravi wears a white coat.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I says every doctor wears a white coat, and statement II says Ravi wears one, but that does not make Ravi a doctor, since others can wear white coats too. Affirming the consequent is the trap: the two statements together still do not settle it, so they are not sufficient.

items.question: Is K the nephew of L? Statement I: K is the son of M. Statement II: M is the sister of L.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only that K is M's son, and statement II gives only that M is L's sister. Together they make K the son of L's sister, which is the definition of a nephew, so both statements together are sufficient. Either statement alone leaves the chain open.

items.question: What is the selling price of an article? Statement I: The profit is 25% of the cost price. Statement II: The profit is Rs. 100.
options: Neither statement alone nor together is sufficient
items.explanation: Statement I gives only the profit as a share of the cost price, and statement II gives only the profit in rupees. Together they give the cost price as 400 and the selling price as 500, so both statements together are sufficient. Either statement alone leaves the other half unknown.

items.question: If the figure for Shimla rises by 20% and the figure for Manali falls by 20%, what is their new combined total?

diagram.caption: Tourists visiting five hill stations in a month (in thousands)

items.explanation: The revised Shimla figure is 54 and the revised Manali figure is 48, so their combined total is 102. Adding the original figures, or revising only one of them, gives the other options.

items.question: The figure for Darjeeling is 70% of its target. If the target is then raised by 20%, what is the new target?
items.explanation: The figure is 35, which is 70% of the target, so the target is 35 x 100 / 70 = 50. Raising it by 20% gives 50 x 1.20 = 60. Taking the old target, or using the figure itself, gives the other options.

items.question: For Shimla and Darjeeling, the given figures are the numbers that succeeded, at success rates of 90% and 70% respectively. If 10% of all attempts for the two together ended in a draw, how many attempts ended in defeat for the two together?
items.explanation: Invert each success rate: Shimla needed 45 x 100 / 90, which is 50 attempts, and Darjeeling needed 50 attempts, giving 100 in all. 10% of these, which is 10, ended in a draw, and 80 were successes, so the defeats are 100 minus 10 minus 80, which is 10. Forgetting the draws, or applying the draw rate to the successes, gives the other options.

items.question: How many more units must Darjeeling add to equal the average of all 5 categories?
items.explanation: The average of the 5 categories is 230 divided by 5, which is 46. The smallest, Darjeeling at 35, needs 11 more to reach it. Answering with the average itself, or with the gap to the largest category, gives the other options.

items.question: If the total of the first 3 categories falls by 10% and the total of the remaining categories rises by 10%, what is the ratio of the revised first total to the revised second total?
items.explanation: The first total is 140, which falls by 10% to 126, and the second total is 90, which rises by 10% to 99. The ratio of 126 to 99 simplifies to 14 : 11. Using the original totals, or reversing the ratio, gives the other options.

items.question: If the total monthly spending rises to Rs. 100000 and Rent's share falls by 5 percentage points, how much is spent on Food and Rent together?
items.explanation: Food is 30% of Rs. 100000, which is Rs. 30000. Rent's share falls from 25% to 20%, so Rent costs 20% of Rs. 100000, which is Rs. 20000. Together they cost Rs. 50000. Using the old Rent share, or taking only one category, gives the other options.

items.question: If spending on Food rises by 10% and spending on Education falls by 10%, by how many rupees does spending on Food exceed spending on Education?
items.explanation: After the changes, Food costs Rs. 26400 and Education costs Rs. 14400, so the gap is Rs. 12000. Changing only one category, or using the original amounts, gives the other options.

items.question: The family wants to keep its spending on Food unchanged in rupees while the total spending rises by 20%. What is Food's new share of the total?
items.explanation: Food spending stays at Rs. 24000 while the total becomes Rs. 96000, so the new share is 24000 divided by 96000, which is 25%. Keeping the share unchanged, or raising the spending with the total, gives the other options.

items.question: Savings are doubled, and the increase is taken equally from Food and Rent. What is the new amount spent on Food?
items.explanation: Doubling savings adds Rs. 8000, so Food and Rent each give up Rs. 4000. Food therefore falls from Rs. 24000 to Rs. 20000. Taking the whole increase from one category, or changing nothing, gives the other options.

items.question: If the total spending rises by 20% and the share spent on Education rises from 20% to 25%, by what percentage does spending on Education rise?
items.explanation: Education spending is Rs. 16000 now and Rs. 24000 after the changes, since the new total is Rs. 96000 and 25% of it is 24000. The rise is 50%. Counting only the total rise, or only the share rise, gives the other options.

items.question: In which year did the value show its highest percentage growth over the previous year, and what was that percentage?

diagram.caption: Books borrowed from a library, 2019 to 2023

items.explanation: The growth rates are 2020: +21.4%, 2021: -26.5%, 2022: +52% and 2023: +15.8%. The highest percentage growth was in 2022, at 52%. Using the largest absolute rise, or the wrong year, gives the other options.

items.question: What is the ratio of the average of the first three years to the average of the last two years?
items.explanation: The first three years average 1450 and the last two average 2050, so the ratio is 29 : 41. Reversing the ratio, or comparing totals instead of averages, gives the other options.

items.question: The chart figures are not all exact. Some years' figures are understated, each by exactly 10% below its true value, and the rest are exact. The true total over the five years is 8850 books. Which of the following must be true?
options: At least one of the 2019 and 2020 figures is understated.
Both the 2019 and 2023 figures are understated.
items.explanation: The chart total is 8450, so the understated figures fall short of their true values by 400 in all. A figure understated by 10% falls short of its true value by one-ninth of the chart figure, so the chart figures of the understated years must add to 3600. Only two pairs do: 2019 and 2023 (1400 + 2200) and 2020 and 2022 (1700 + 1900). Both pairs contain 2019 or 2020, so at least one of those two years must be understated. The 2021 figure is understated in neither pair; 2023 and 2022 each appear in only one pair, so neither must be understated; and the 2019 and 2023 pair is only one of the two possibilities.

items.question: By what percentage is the highest value more than the lowest value, after the lowest value is revised up by 10%?
items.explanation: The lowest value becomes 1375 after the 10% revision, and the highest is 2200, so the gap is 60% of the revised lowest value. Ignoring the revision, or using the highest value as the base, gives the other options.

items.question: The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes is one way to describe the growth of books borrowed between 2019 and 2023. The compound annual growth rate over the same period is another. Which of the following is true?
options: The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes is greater than the compound annual growth rate over the same period.
The compound annual growth rate exceeds 20%.
The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes is less than 10%.
The compound annual growth rate equals the average yearly absolute change divided by the 2019 figure.
The average of the four year-on-year percentage changes equals 20%.
items.explanation: The year-on-year changes are +21.4% in 2020, -26.5% in 2021, +52% in 2022 and +15.8% in 2023, and their average is about 15.7%. The number rose from 1400 to 2200 over four years, so the compound annual growth rate is the fourth root of 2200/1400 minus 1, about 12.0%. The average of the yearly percentage changes is therefore greater than the compound rate. The compound rate is below 20%, the average is above 10%, and the average yearly absolute change divided by the 2019 figure is 200/1400, or 14.3%, which is not the compound rate.
